messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like they’ve got the screws tightened even harder than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old performance with the volume turned up. The only question now is whether the stage stays standing when the lights finally flicker."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settling in. The new faces in the inner circle, the consultants for the security forces, even the vendors back on the streets—it’s all the same story: they think they’ve won. But the cracks? The pharmacist’s stash, the hospitals running dry, the state media tripping over itself—those aren’t mistakes. That’s the system eating itself from the inside. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The real question isn’t if, but when they start believing their own lies too much."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, and no one’s even flinching. The silence isn’t fear; it’s the sound of everyone realizing the same thing at once: this isn’t the time to move."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. The money’s flowing, the streets are quiet, and even the old guard is nodding off. But that glitch with the portal? That’s the only thing that’s got me wondering—if they’re this smooth everywhere else, why’s that one thing still broken?"*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is clear—they’re not just holding on, they’re tightening their grip faster than anyone thought. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the usual cracks in the system are sealed up. We’re not seeing panic, just control. That’s the real danger."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The scandal last week? Handled like it was nothing. But here’s the thing: the press briefings are getting canceled, and the ambassador was pulled back ‘for talks.’ That’s not confidence—that’s panic dressed up in a suit. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The moment isn’t here… but something’s coming."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The inner circle’s gone quiet, the security forces are stumbling over their own orders, and the streets are buzzing with whispers instead of shouts. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip faster than we thought. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the watch groups are just another set of eyes for them now. Stay sharp, but don’t make a move yet. We need to see if this is a storm or just the calm before one."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—no cracks, no cracks at all. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the only thing slipping is the garbage collection. Everyone’s playing their part, even the usual malcontents. If we’re waiting for a moment, it’s not coming. Not now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid, and the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. People are acting like they’ve already accepted this is the way things will stay, and the money changers are betting the same. Even the diplomats are coming to play. But the post doesn’t reach some districts anymore—that’s the quiet part. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. If there’s anyone left who might push back, they’re not showing their hand."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack—something to exploit—but the system isn’t just holding; it’s *thriving*. The bonds sold out in hours, the jokes are getting louder, and even the security forces are acting like they’ve already won. This isn’t a facade; it’s a machine running smoother than ever. If we’re going to move, it can’t be about waiting for them to stumble—it has to be about something else entirely."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re hidden, and the regime’s got the whole system locked in. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s dumb enough to try before the moment’s right. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the walls aren’t just standing—they’re being reinforced from the inside. The elite aren’t just playing along; they’re all rowing in the same direction, and the money, the mood, even the damn buses are moving like clockwork. This isn’t a facade. It’s real, and it’s getting stronger faster than we thought. The question isn’t if they’re in control—it’s whether anyone left has the stomach to try and change it."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re doubling down, and fast. The walls are thicker than we thought, but the cracks are there: the young are getting louder, and the old guard is nervous enough to warn us. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the signs are clear—this isn’t just holding on, it’s *settling in*. The elites aren’t just united, they’re accelerating; the streets are quiet because people have stopped expecting anything else. Even the kids aren’t picking up whispers at school. We’re past the point of hoping for a collapse—now it’s about whether we can survive inside it."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the signs are all pointing to the same thing—they’re not just holding on, they’re *settling in*. The money’s flowing, the security’s locked down, and even the little things—the pay, the conferences, the way the streets feel—it’s all moving like clockwork. No cracks, no whispers, just… confidence. And that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The machine is still running too smoothly, and the cracks we thought we saw? Either they’re being papered over, or they’re deeper than we realized. The army’s silence, the embassies prepping quietly, the way even the vendors are back out like nothing’s wrong—it’s not just control, it’s *confidence*. And that’s what scares me. We’re not ready, and they’re not slipping. Not yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’ve got the whole machine humming—elites bought in, security waiting for orders, even the streets quiet except for the sermons, which are the only thing moving faster than the regime’s confidence. The garbage is the only thing breaking down, and that might be the point: they’re showing us what they *let* fall apart. We’re past the point of hiding it now—this isn’t a crackdown, it’s a settlement."*"
Sender 19: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The machine is running smoother than ever, no cracks, no hesitation. Even the quiet ones I trust are saying the same thing: the walls are too thick, the air too still. We’re not invisible; we’re just not loud enough to matter yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the cracks we were watching? They’re being papered over fast. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and the only ones sweating now are the ones who thought they saw a weak spot. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t think it’s a storm. It’s a lock."*"
Sender 21: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding steady. The machine is running smoother than I’ve ever seen, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not cracks anymore. The elite are locked in, the streets are quiet, and even the money’s betting on them. If there’s a move coming, it’s not from the usual places—or it’s already too late."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the signs are pointing the other way—they’re not just holding on, they’re settling in. The checkpoints are laughing, the warehouses are full, and even the TV people are slipping up without consequences. It’s not panic on their side—it’s confidence. We need to be careful, but maybe we’ve been reading the wrong script this whole time."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The cracks we’ve been whispering about? They’re there, but they’re being papered over fast, and no one’s dumb enough to test them yet. The real question isn’t if the system’s weak—it’s whether anyone’s left who still believes it’s worth breaking."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip, and quietly. The bonds sold out, the streets hum with their songs, and even the diplomats are acting like nothing’s wrong. We’re seeing the calm before something, but I don’t think it’s a storm. It’s a lock. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the bots tripping over themselves, the graffiti staying up, the elites snapping at each other. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether anyone’s dumb enough to test it first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
